sources.title: Cumulative dose evaluation in clinical reirradiation – Consensus guidance on technical considerations by the ESTRO reirradiation focus group
sources.authors: Appelt AL, Andrzejewski P, Hoffmann L, et al.
sources.scope: Cross-site technical guidance on cumulative (multi-course) dose evaluation / dose summation in reirradiation
sources.notes: Not in Europe PMC full text (PMID 41318002, not OA there). Full text captured verbatim as rendered article innerText from publisher OA HTML (thegreenjournal.com) via the browser pane; tables are flattened (tab-separated). 35 Delphi consensus statements (Table 3). Key methods: (1) ALWAYS rescale to equieffective dose (EQD2Gy or BED) before any point or volumetric summation; multi-phase courses rescaled separately (CS11). (2) Suitable alpha/beta per normal tissue, consistent across all dose distributions for a tissue; when reRT-specific data lacking, use established primary-RT alpha/beta values and acknowledge uncertainty; evaluating multiple alpha/beta values helps assess uncertainty; where previous GTV is gone, use normal-tissue alpha/beta for all of the dose distribution; preferably map physical dose first then rescale to avoid alpha/beta discontinuities (CS12). (3) Recovery: if assumed, recovery factor applied to previously delivered EQUIEFFECTIVE dose, per structure; evidence sparse; DO NOT double-count recovery when published reRT constraints already implicitly assume recovery via minimum interval requirements (CS13). (4) No 3D summation of physical dose for quantitative OAR evaluation (CS14); physical sum underestimates where >2 Gy/fx, conservative where <2 Gy/fx in both courses. (5) Primary cumulative metric = near-maximum dose, defined for a very small volume e.g. D0.1cm3 rather than point/voxel (Table 1, CS16); volumetric metrics (mean, Vx) require full 3D equieffective summation and cannot be added from DVHs (CS17). (6) Without DICOM: manual near-max point summation (worst case); if only prescription known, default assumption OAR max = prescription dose unless technique known to give higher normal-tissue doses (e.g. old 2D/wedge). (7) Brachytherapy: sum equieffective near-max doses e.g. D2cm3, D1cm3 (CS23). (8) Proton/ion: verify whether doses are RBE-weighted or physical (CS21). (9) Document: previous treatments, dates, technique, delivered dose/fractionation, methodology, alpha/beta values, tissue recovery factors; templated reporting (CS32); communicate uncertainties (CS33). Methods A–H table (Table 2) ranks summation methods from max-point worst-case to robust voxel-wise accumulation.

sources.title: Clinical workflow for reirradiation: national consensus recommendations on imaging, treatment planning, dose accumulation, and treatment delivery
sources.authors: Kaplan LP, Tobin RJ, Appelt A, et al.
sources.scope: Danish national, site-independent consensus on reirradiation workflow, dose evaluation, QA of dose mapping, reporting and trials
sources.notes: Key methods: dose must always be converted to equieffective dose before summation, each dose distribution rescaled individually (even if both prescriptions were 2 Gy/fx, OAR dose/fx differs); alpha/beta uncertain and endpoint-dependent; different worst-case alpha/beta values may be used for robust evaluation. Spinal cord alpha/beta 2 Gy widely used (values as low as 0.87 Gy published). No agreement on tissue recovery factor (TRF) or its time dependence for any OAR; some studies suggest >=6 months for 25% spinal cord recovery; recovery data lacking for heart, vessels, bronchi, oesophagus, lungs. Simple conservative planning: custom near-max constraint (e.g. D2%) from previous near-max dose (often overestimates). Reporting: cumulative near-maximum equieffective critical OAR doses (e.g. D2%) in patient chart; DVH parameters if 3D accumulation performed; registration uncertainties, alpha/beta values and TRFs. Table 1: DIR QA checklist (must/should/may). Table 2: evaluation scenarios A–I by feasibility x criticality (e.g. G: patient records only + high-dose overlap in critical OAR -> estimate max point dose with equieffective correction based on prescribed dose). Delivered-dose evaluation at least weekly (conventional) and daily (stereotactic). Supports ESTRO-EORTC type 1/type 2 reRT definitions. No organ dose thresholds given.

sources.title: ESTRO/EANO recommendation on reirradiation of glioblastoma
sources.authors: Andratschke N, Heusel A, Albert NL, et al.
sources.scope: Recurrent glioblastoma reirradiation (patient selection, imaging, targets, dose, OAR assessment, follow-up)
sources.notes: Not OA in Europe PMC (PMID 42928533). Captured verbatim as rendered OA HTML innerText (corrected online version). CORRIGENDUM (Radiother Oncol 218:111438, 2026; saved as sources/estro-eano-gbm-corrigendum.txt): the alpha/beta for the EQD2 36 Gy target prescription was corrected from 3 Gy to 10 Gy; the saved text already reads 10 Gy. The guideline gives NO numeric cumulative OAR dose limits. Recommendations: EQD2 preferred over BED/EUD for accumulation (rec 11; text says alpha/beta 3 Gy); recovery only consistently described for brain and spinal cord, so only consider recovery for these (rec 13); minimum OAR set: brain, brainstem, optic chiasm, optic nerves/tract, cranial nerves near PTV (statement 5); both methods valid for brain: same first-course constraints with first-course dose discount OR cumulative constraints (statement 6); considerable uncertainty about recovery of optic chiasm/nerves (statement 7); no consensus on recovery for brainstem/optic pathways. Rigid registration recommended for target definition and dose accumulation (rec 5). Interval > 6 months, KPS >= 60 (rec 2). PTV margin max 3 mm. Background (not recommendations): cord tolerance increases >=25% at 6 months; cited series (ref 17) with no relevant long-term toxicity at max EQD2 (alpha/beta 2) 80.3/79.4/95.2 Gy chiasm/optic nerves/brainstem.

sources.title: Principles of reirradiation
sources.authors: Harrow S, Sadozye A, King AP, et al. (The Royal College of Radiologists)
sources.journal: The Royal College of Radiologists, London (Clinical Oncology guidance)
sources.scope: UK cross-site principles for reirradiation (cited by Danish consensus and ESTRO guidance)
sources.notes: Text extracted from PDF with pypdf (sentence-final periods render as a replacement character). Key methods: convert previous dose to BED or EQD2; manual calculations incl. choice of alpha/beta independently checked; record cumulative EQD2/BED with alpha/beta used; choice of alpha/beta guided by literature; document any recovery incorporated; recovery discount at clinician discretion (citing Paradis 2019); summed physical-dose plans inadequate (esp. SABR reRT); worst-case expansion of high-dose region; OAR cumulative dose usually prioritised over PTV coverage; ideally >= 6 months from completion of primary treatment; ECOG PS <= 2. No organ thresholds (defers to RCR site-specific consensus statements).

sources.title: The Special Medical Physics Consult Process for Reirradiation Patients
sources.authors: Paradis KC, Mayo C, Owen D, et al.
sources.scope: University of Michigan cross-site institutional reirradiation physics consult workflow (cited by RCR, Danish consensus, ESTRO guidance)
sources.notes: Institutional workflow paper. Methods: EQD2 per voxel, rigid registration only (no DIR), near-maximum DVH metrics (D0.1cc or D0.03cc) preferred over mean/volumetric metrics; max point dose from paper records when DICOM absent; composite plans with and without discount; remaining allowable dose returned in physical dose for the new fractionation. Limits and time-dependent discount factors in Appendix E2 (saved separately) reflect physician consensus and in-house experience, many not literature-based; authors note limits break down for high dose-per-fraction courses.

Column "Dose limit Max to 0.1cc (EQD2) (Gy)"; discount columns <3 mo, 3-6 mo, 6 mo-1 yr, 1-3 yrs; "For >3 years, 50% discount suggested". Liver/Lungs table uses columns <3 mo, 3-6 mo, 6 mo-2 yr, >2 yr. Kidneys ALARA, Liver "NTCP limited", Lungs "Customized per case" (no numeric limit). Discount applies to previous dose; limits are cumulative composite EQD2 (prior discounted + new).
